result.headline: Roll-control outputs ch4/ch5 froze at neutral 1500 at t=65.92 s; roll and yaw tracking then failed.
result.explanation: A control fault occurred: the ch4/ch5 output pair went flat at 1500 from t=65.92 s to the end while the roll loop still moved. The recording cannot show whether the controller output or the servo hardware failed.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[4]] held 1500 from t=65.92 to 101.49 s (109 samples)
evidence.shows: ch4 was moving, then held neutral for the remaining 35.6 s. No mode change or event explains it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[5]] held 1500 from t=65.92 to 101.49 s (109 samples)
evidence.shows: ch5 froze together with ch4. Before the freeze ch4 and ch5 were identical (correlation 1.0, difference 0 us), so they are one paired output.

evidence.quote: SHIFT control.attitude_setpoint[roll] changed level for good at t=67.743 s: median 7.84 before, 42.03 after deg (7.4x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The roll setpoint moved to about 42 deg after the freeze. At t=77.3 it flipped from 44.87 to -44.85 deg and roll tracking error rose about 7.8x (4.72 to 36.803 deg).

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[3]] follows control.attitude_setpoint[roll] (correlation 0.834 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch3 serves the roll loop and kept moving after the freeze (1580 to 1364 us at t=77.3). Only the ch4/ch5 pair stopped.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a3 t=65.92 s: actuator.output[ch[4]] was moving, then held 1500 for 35.57 s (see line 25; strength 3.908)
evidence.shows: The freeze is the one output frozen with no operator or mode event, and the only mid-flight output that stopped moving.

checked.check: Sequence of departures from baseline over 50-90 s
checked.result: The roll setpoint left baseline at 58.249 s, ch3/ch4/ch5 at 58.38 s, and roll attitude followed at 59.917 s. The setpoint came first, which suggests a manoeuvre rather than an output fault.

checked.check: Compare at the roll tracking candidate, t=56.523 s
checked.result: Roll error rose 11.07x, but the setpoint stepped at the same time. In the 54-70 s window, roll attitude follows the setpoint with a lag (setpoint 44.88 at 60.819 s, attitude 44.602 at 62.147 s). This is manoeuvre lag, not a fault.
checked.about: Setpoint or estimator as the cause

checked.check: Compare at the ch4/ch5 freeze, t=65.92 s
checked.result: Both outputs froze (spread 24.5 to 0). Roll tracking error was 5.989 before and 7.407 after, so the freeze itself was not an abrupt break in tracking.

checked.check: Compare at the later divergence, t=77.3 s
checked.result: The roll setpoint flipped from 44.87 to -44.85 deg, ch3 swung from 1580 to 1364 us, and roll and yaw errors rose about 7.8x and 7.42x (roll 4.72 to 36.803 deg). Roll did not follow the flipped setpoint even though ch3 moved. This is consistent with lost roll authority on the ch4/ch5 pair.

checked.check: Compare at t=93.3 s and the shifts at t=84.872 s and t=93.245 s
checked.result: Roll tracking error fell from 41.022 to 12.125 deg after 93.3 s. Throttle shifted at 93.245 s and ch3 at 84.872 s. These look like late effects or recovery attempts, not the onset.

checked.check: Compare at the t=20.509 s velocity[y] shift
checked.result: Velocity[y] stepped from -15.62 to -0.62 m/s while tracking was unchanged or better (yaw error ratio 0.23). This is a manoeuvre.
checked.about: Early velocity shift as a fault

checked.result: The only events are the start-up lines at t=0.538 s: 'WARN: Low voltage' and 'ERROR: Sensor helth'. Nothing appears in the event list at the time of the freeze. There are no lessons.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a7 t=77.438 s: vehicle.attitude[roll] followed control.attitude_setpoint[roll] worse for good (typical |error| 4.71 -> 19.111)
effects.why: Roll tracking got worse after the ch4/ch5 freeze, and ch3 alone did not hold it.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a8 t=78.308 s: vehicle.attitude[yaw] followed control.attitude_setpoint[yaw] worse for good (typical |error| 7.708 -> 93.401)
effects.why: Yaw error comes after the freeze and the roll loss. The yaw setpoint is unwrapped (392-649 deg) while attitude is wrapped, so part of this error may be an angle-wrap artefact.

effects.quote: SHIFT propulsion.throttle changed level for good at t=93.245 s: median 49 before, 67 after %
effects.why: Throttle, ch1, ch2 and roll attitude shifted late, which looks like compensation or the aircraft departing.

next_action.action: Bench-test ch4/ch5 with props off: command roll and read the PWM and the servos.
next_action.why: Separates a frozen controller output from a servo or wiring fault on the ch4/ch5 pair. The recorded PWM is a command, not the servo's position.
how: Put the autopilot on the bench with the propeller removed.
Move the roll input through its range and read the PWM on ch3, ch4 and ch5 in the ground station.
If the PWM on ch4/ch5 moves, put a scope or servo tester on the ch4/ch5 output pins and watch the servos.
Check the flight controller log for output failsafe or mixer-disable flags near the freeze time.
next_action.conditions: Bench, powered, motor disarmed, props off, same firmware and mixer configuration as flight 28, with roll commanded through its full range.
next_action.baseline: ch3 following roll, and ch4/ch5 moving in sync before the freeze (lines 31-33, cc_11).

outcomes.label: PWM frozen at 1500 on ch4/ch5
outcomes.means: The fault is in the controller, mixer or output stage. The command stopped before the hardware.
outcomes.then: Inspect the mixer config, firmware and failsafe log for the output freeze.

outcomes.label: PWM moves but servos do not
outcomes.means: The servo, wiring or driver for the ch4/ch5 pair is faulty. In flight the frozen commands could be a symptom.
outcomes.then: Replace the servo or harness and repeat the flight-profile test.

outcomes.label: Everything moves normally on the bench
outcomes.means: The freeze needs flight conditions, such as a load, brown-out or software state. Compare the flight log at the freeze time.
outcomes.then: Request the full flight-controller log and repeat under load.

unknowns: Who or what commanded ch4/ch5 to 1500 at t=65.92 s. The recording shows no mode change or event there.
Whether the servos on ch4/ch5 physically moved. Only the commanded PWM is recorded.
Whether the large yaw error is real or an angle-wrap artefact of the unwrapped yaw setpoint.

already_answered.question: Did a control fault occur, and when?

unobservable.why_it_matters: A servo, wiring or linkage fault cannot be told apart from a controller output freeze using the commanded PWM alone.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench actuation, a visual and mechanical inspection, and a servo rail voltage check.

hypotheses.claim: The flight controller or mixer stopped updating the ch4/ch5 outputs and held neutral 1500.
hypotheses.because: The pair went flat at 1500 for 35.6 s with no event, while ch3 and the other outputs kept moving.

hypotheses.claim: The servos, wiring or driver for the ch4/ch5 pair failed, and the frozen commands are a symptom.
hypotheses.because: The recording holds only commanded PWM, so a servo-side fault is neither shown nor excluded.

hypotheses.claim: The roll setpoint and guidance saturated or flipped, and the aircraft could not follow.
hypotheses.because: The setpoint shift (67.7 s) and flip (77.3 s) came after the freeze, and roll followed the setpoint with a lag before it.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor or estimator fault produced bad attitude readings.
hypotheses.because: Roll followed the setpoint before the freeze. The only sensor-health line is at start-up (0.538 s). airspeed and yaw_rate are constant at 0 for the whole recording, so they gave no information.

hypotheses.claim: A voltage drop caused the output freeze.
hypotheses.because: The only battery line is the start-up warning at 0.538 s. No battery voltage signal is in this recording, so power can be neither supported nor excluded.

events.what: ch4 and ch5 froze at 1500 from t=65.92 s
events.why: One paired output stopped while the others kept moving, with no event explaining it.

events.what: Roll setpoint shifted to about 42 deg at 67.7 s
events.why: A change after the freeze, with a flip to -45 deg at 77.3 s.

events.what: Roll and yaw tracking got worse from t=77 s
events.why: Follows the freeze and the setpoint flip. Part of the yaw error may come from angle wrap.

events.what: Late shifts in ch1, ch2, ch3, throttle and roll at 84-93 s
events.why: Compensation or the aircraft departing after the loss of roll authority.

events.what: Low voltage warning and sensor health error at t=0.538 s
events.why: Start-up lines. Nothing later changes in them.
